decks.notes: The deck focuses on assembling a toolbox of creatures to combo off and control the game. Utilizing cards like Chord of Calling and Eldritch Evolution, the deck can search for specific creatures to fit the situation. Creatures like Yawgmoth, Thran Physician, Grist, the Hunger Tide, and Sheoldred, the Apocalypse provide powerful effects that can disrupt the opponent or generate value for the player. With the help of mana dorks like Birds of Paradise and Ignoble Hierarch, the deck aims to efficiently ramp into its combo pieces and overwhelm the opponent with its creature synergy.

This deck focuses on utilizing the Indomitable Creativity card to cheat out powerful creatures like Archon of Cruelty, creating a powerful combo with Persist. The deck also includes cards like Wrenn and Six to help with card advantage and recursion. The goal is to set up a board state where the opponent is overwhelmed by high-impact creatures and is unable to recover. The deck also includes disruption cards like Inquisition of Kozilek to disrupt the opponent's game plan and clear the way for the combo to take over the game.

The deck focuses on fast, aggressive plays using a combination of disruptive hand disruption spells like Thoughtseize, powerful threats like Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer, and synergistic cards like Dauthi Voidwalker and Feign Death to overwhelm opponents quickly. The deck also includes disruptive elements like Blood Moon and removal spells like Fatal Push and Terminate to control the board and prevent opponents from stabilizing. Overall, the deck aims to apply early pressure, disrupt opponents' game plans, and close out games before they have a chance to recover.

The deck focuses on using cards like Indomitable Creativity and Dwarven Mine to quickly bring out powerful creatures like Archon of Cruelty and combo pieces like Fable of the Mirror-Breaker. Teferi, Time Raveler and Wrenn and Six provide utility and control options, while mana fixing is achieved through various fetch lands and triomes. Spell Pierce and Mana Leak help protect the combo pieces and disrupt opponents' strategies, while Lightning Bolt and Prismari Command provide versatile removal options. The deck aims to creatively assemble its combo pieces to overwhelm the opponent and secure victory.

This deck focuses on quickly overwhelming the opponent with aggressive creatures and efficient removal spells. The key strategy is to play low-cost creatures like Wild Nacatl and Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer, while using Tribal Flames and Lightning Bolt to control the board and deal direct damage. The deck also features powerful late-game threats like Scion of Draco and Migloz, Maze Crusher to ensure the pressure stays on the opponent. With the use of Jegantha, the Wellspring as a companion, the deck is able to maintain consistency and generate additional mana for its spells.

This Rakdos Aggro deck focuses on aggressive plays and disruption. It utilizes cards like Thoughtseize, Grief, and Dauthi Voidwalker to disrupt the opponent's hand and board state, while cards like Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer and Seasoned Pyromancer provide aggressive threats. The deck also includes removal spells like Terminate and Fatal Push to deal with opposing creatures. Overall, the key concept of this deck is to apply pressure on the opponent early on while disrupting their game plan, aiming to close out the game quickly.

The main concept of this deck is to use Cascade mechanics to quickly and aggressively put pressure on the opponent. By casting cards with Cascade, such as Violent Outburst and Shardless Agent, the player can potentially cast additional spells for free, overwhelming the opponent with threats. The deck also utilizes cards like Dead / Gone and Fire / Ice for removal and disruption, while including counterspells like Force of Negation and Mystical Dispute for protection. The land base includes fetch lands and multicolor lands to ensure consistent mana fixing for the deck's diverse requirements.

The deck focuses on aggressive plays using efficient creatures like Tarmogoyf and Ragavan, combined with burn spells like Lightning Bolt and Fury to put pressure on the opponent. It also includes disruption in the form of hand disruption spells like Inquisition of Kozilek and Thoughtseize, as well as removal spells like Terminate and Fatal Push. The deck utilizes the Jund color combination for a versatile range of threats and answers, with cards like Kroxa, Titan of Death's Hunger and Liliana of the Veil providing additional value and disruption.

This deck focuses on aggressive plays supported by a mix of powerful creatures and efficient removal spells. The key strategy involves quickly establishing a board presence with early drops like Wild Nacatl and Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer, backed up by burn spells like Lightning Bolt and Tribal Flames. The deck aims to close out the game swiftly by overwhelming the opponent with threats and finishing them off with direct damage. Additionally, the use of Jegantha, the Wellspring as a companion provides extra value and flexibility to the deck's game plan.

This UR Aggro deck focuses on quickly deploying low-cost creatures like Soul-Scar Mage, Monastery Swiftspear, and Dragon's Rage Channeler to apply early pressure on the opponent. Utilizing cheap removal spells like Lightning Bolt and Vapor Snag, along with efficient card draw spells such as Light Up the Stage and Expressive Iteration, the deck aims to maintain a steady stream of threats while disrupting the opponent's game plan. The inclusion of Mishra's Bauble and Underworld Breach adds additional card advantage and combo potential, allowing the deck to maintain its aggression throughout the game.

The main concept of this deck is to quickly deploy threats such as Murktide Regent, Dragon's Rage Channeler, and Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer while disrupting the opponent's game plan with cards like Lightning Bolt and Spell Pierce. The deck aims to apply early pressure and maintain tempo advantage through efficient spells, card selection with Mishra's Bauble and Expressive Iteration, and disruption with Counterspell and Unholy Heat. The mana base is optimized to support the aggressive gameplay while also providing some flexibility with fetch lands. Overall, the deck focuses on a proactive and fast-paced approach to win the game.

This deck aims to quickly cycle through cards in order to play Living End to bring back powerful creatures from the graveyard and overwhelm the opponent with a sudden army. The key strategy is to manipulate the graveyard and control the board until you can cast Living End and swing the game in your favor. Using cards like Architects of Will and Grief to disrupt the opponent's hand and creatures, while cycling through your own deck with Street Wraith and Curator of Mysteries, sets up the perfect conditions for a devastating Living End combo.

This deck focuses on assembling the UrzaTron lands - Urza's Mine, Urza's Tower, and Urza's Power Plant - to generate massive amounts of mana. The key concept revolves around using this mana to cast powerful colorless spells like Karn Liberated, Ulamog, the Ceaseless Hunger, and Ugin, the Spirit Dragon, while controlling the board with cards like Oblivion Stone and Walking Ballista. The deck aims to outvalue opponents by utilizing its mana advantage and powerful threats to dominate the game.

The deck focuses on assembling the UrzaTron lands to generate a large amount of colorless mana, allowing the player to cast powerful threats like Wurmcoil Engine, Ulamog, and Karn Liberated. The deck also includes various utility cards like Oblivion Stone and Relic of Progenitus to control the board and disrupt opponent's strategies. The inclusion of Jegantha as a companion adds an additional threat and mana source. The goal is to control the game with big threats and overwhelming mana advantage from the UrzaTron lands.

This deck focuses on quickly ramping up mana to cast powerful spells like Primeval Titan and Cultivator Colossus. It utilizes cards like Amulet of Vigor and Dryad of the Ilysian Grove to accelerate mana production and enable big plays. The deck also includes utility lands like Urza's Saga and Sunhome, Fortress of the Legion for additional value. The key goal is to assemble the Amulet Titan combo to generate overwhelming board presence and overwhelm the opponent with big creatures and powerful effects.

The main concept of this deck is to quickly cycle through cards to power out Living End, a powerful sorcery that allows you to wipe the board of creatures and bring back your own powerful creatures from the graveyard. This archetype focuses on setting up the perfect combination of cards to create a massive swing in tempo and advantage, overwhelming your opponent with a sudden board presence. Using a mix of cycling creatures and cascade spells, the deck aims to disrupt your opponent's game plan while setting up your own win condition.
